newsitem.title: USA: United American sees Q4 below consensus.
newsitem.headline: United American sees Q4 below consensus.

text.p: United American Healthcare Corp said the company expects earnings for the June 30 fourth quarter and full year to be significantly below analyst estimates.
United American Healthcare said it filed for an extension in filing its Form 10-K annual report, normally due on September 30.

It said the need for an extension was brought on by a delay in completing an audit of the company's OmniCare Health Plan Inc subsidiary in Tennessee and the pursuit of third-party financing by its New York joint venture, United HealthScope Inc, which is expected to be completed on or about October 3.
The company did not give a date for the completion of the audit. The company expects to report results by October 14.
A spokesman for United American Healthcare, a healthcare management company, said the analysts' consensus for the fourth quarter was for earnings in a range of $0.22 to $0.33 per share.

For the full year, the consensus ranged from a loss of $0.04 to profit of $0.07 per year, the company said. In 1995, the company had actual earnings for the full year of $1.01/shr and actual loss of $0.10 /shr for Q4.

"Despite our anticipated shortfall from preliminary estimates, we continue to be enthusiastic about our prospects for growth in membership," said Julius Combs, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.
